SMTO-PRL-0002 — SMTO couldn't find that step in this task

GUID: 813f1e5a-f158-4af9-a85d-d811d726c4fc
Slug: activity-not-found
Domain: PRL · Subsystem: prl

What happened

  • The step you tried to stop or answer isn't part of this task any more, or the page was showing an old view. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page in your browser, then reopen this conversation. The page may have been showing a step that has since finished or been replaced.
  2. Open the Activities section under the task and find the step again. Only steps listed there now can be stopped or answered.
  3. If the step is no longer listed, read its result in the conversation instead. A step that has finished has no controls left to use.

What success looks like

  • The step appears in the Activities section and its button works without an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't use the controls on a different step in its place.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An activity control request named an activity_id that is not present in the run's background, dependency or foreground-batch activity records.

What this means

  • Background activity selection cannot find the requested activity among this run's available activity records. Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.

Why this can happen

  • Background activity selection cannot find the requested activity among this run's available activity records.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh the owning run's current activity inventory and verify the requested ID.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the run snapshot and target an activity_id currently listed in the run's background_activities, dependency_activities or foreground_batch. Do not redirect the control to a different activity or run.
  • Refresh the run’s activity list and select an activity from its current owning run.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The control targets a currently observed activity in the intended run.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
